key_insight: Gate3DGen selectively cleans up real-world images before they reach a 3D generator, while leaving clean inputs unchanged. It improves input preparation without retraining the downstream generator.
problem_solved: Single-image 3D generators perform well on curated images but struggle with uneven lighting, blur, and occlusions. Pre-processing must address these degradations without removing visual cues needed to reconstruct 3D objects.
method: Use a degradation-aware router to decide whether an input needs purification or should bypass processing.
Selectively purify degraded inputs while preserving visual information needed for 3D generation.
Pass the resulting image to an existing 3D generator without retraining it.
impact: This approach offers practitioners a way to adapt existing 3D-generation pipelines to less-controlled images while avoiding unnecessary changes to clean inputs. The supplied abstract is truncated and does not provide quantitative results.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: input image → degradation-aware router → bypass or purification → existing 3D generator.
Image examples illustrating uneven lighting, blur, and occlusion.
Split-path graphic showing clean inputs preserved and degraded inputs selectively processed.
Object-cue illustration highlighting details that purification should retain for 3D reconstruction.
paper_title: Gate3DGen: A Pre-processing Model that Selectively Purifies Real-World Images for 3D Generation
paper_authors: Xiaolin Li, Zihao Huang, Fanpeng Meng, Chen Yang, Guanjun Wu
